title: Nutty Gooey Greek Eggplant Moussaka
description: A classic Greek dish with a nutty twist, featuring a rich eggplant and meat sauce topped with a gooey, creamy bechamel sauce. This meal-prep recipe is perfect for a weeknight dinner or lunch the next day.

ingredients.name: ground lamb
ingredients.notes: lean option for a milder flavor

ingredients.name: milk
ingredients.notes: whole milk or non-dairy milk alternative

instructions: Brush eggplant slices with olive oil and season with salt. Place on a baking sheet and roast for 20-25 minutes, or until tender and lightly browned.

Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add the chopped onion and cook, stirring occasionally, until lightly browned and fragrant, about 8-10 minutes. Add the minced garlic and cook for an additional 1-2 minutes, stirring constantly.

Add the ground lamb to the skillet, breaking it up with a spoon as it cooks. Cook until the lamb is no longer pink, about 5-7 minutes. Add the tomato paste and cook for 1-2 minutes, stirring constantly. Add the crushed canned tomatoes, cayenne pepper, and salt. Stir to combine and bring the sauce to a simmer.
Reduce heat to medium-low and let the sauce simmer for 10-15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until thickened and flavorful. Meanwhile, prepare the bechamel sauce (see below).

To make the bechamel sauce, melt butter in a medium saucepan over medium heat. Add the all-purpose flour and cook, stirring constantly, for 1-2 minutes, or until the mixture forms a smooth, light brown paste. Slowly pour in the milk, whisking constantly to prevent lumps. Bring the mixture to a simmer and cook, stirring occasionally, until thickened and creamy, about 5-7 minutes. Remove from heat and stir in the nutritional yeast.

To assemble the moussaka, spread a layer of the lamb sauce in the bottom of a 9x13-inch baking dish. Arrange a layer of roasted eggplant slices on top of the sauce. Spread half of the bechamel sauce over the eggplant. Repeat the layers, starting with the lamb sauce, then the eggplant, and finally the remaining bechamel sauce.

Cover the baking dish with aluminum foil and bake for 30 minutes. Remove the foil and continue baking for an additional 10-15 minutes, or until the top is golden brown and the moussaka is heated through.
Remove from the oven and let cool for 10-15 minutes before serving.
Serve hot, garnished with fresh parsley or oregano, if desired.
